scenes.img: Dawn on a palace terrace: Kunti: young princess in a pale blue sari, hands folded, looks up in awe as the Sun god, a radiant figure in gold within a great sun disc, appears in the sky before her.
scenes.text: Long before the great war… a young princess named Kunti was given a mantra that could call any god. Curious, she called the Sun.

scenes.img: Kunti: young princess in a pale blue sari holds a newborn baby wrapped in cloth; the baby already has large gold sun-shaped earrings and a small gold armour plate on his chest, glinting.
scenes.text: And she was given a son… born with golden armour on his chest, and golden earrings, shining like the sun itself.

scenes.img: At night by a river, Kunti: young princess in a pale blue sari, weeping, lets go of a small woven basket carrying a baby, floating away on the dark water.
scenes.text: But Kunti was young, and unmarried, and afraid. She placed the baby in a basket… and let the river carry him away.

scenes.img: Morning at a riverbank: Adhiratha and Radha: a humble charioteer couple in simple brown and orange cotton clothes lift a baby from a woven basket among the reeds, overjoyed; the baby wears gold earrings.
scenes.text: Downstream, a charioteer named Adhiratha and his wife Radha found the basket. They raised the boy as their own… and loved him.

scenes.img: A boy about twelve with dark-brown skin, gold sun-shaped earrings and a small gold armour plate on his chest practises archery alone at dawn, aiming at a target on a tree, many arrows around.
scenes.text: Karna grew up with one dream: to be the greatest archer in the world. He practised from dawn… to dusk.

scenes.img: At the gate of a royal training ground, a stern old teacher in white raises his hand to stop a youth (dark-brown skin, gold sun earrings, gold chest armour plate, simple clothes) from entering, while royal princes practise inside.
scenes.text: But he was a charioteer’s son. The story goes that the royal teacher turned him away. Princes only.

scenes.img: In a mountain hermitage, Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti, now dressed as a humble brahmin student with a sacred thread, bows before Parashurama: old sage, long white beard and matted hair, saffron robe, a large axe beside him.
scenes.text: So he went to the great sage Parashurama, who taught only brahmins… and Karna said he was one.

scenes.img: Afternoon under a tree: Parashurama: old sage, long white beard and matted hair, saffron robe, a large axe beside him sleeps with his head on the lap of Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti; a large insect bites Karna’s thigh and blood runs, but Karna stays perfectly still, enduring the pain.
scenes.text: One afternoon the old teacher slept with his head on Karna’s lap. An insect bit deep into Karna’s thigh. He did not move… so his teacher could rest.

scenes.img: Parashurama: old sage, long white beard and matted hair, saffron robe, a large axe beside him, now awake and angry, points at Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti, who kneels with head bowed; blood on the ground.
scenes.text: Parashurama woke, saw the blood, and knew. No brahmin could bear such pain. Angry at the lie, he cursed him: when you need your knowledge most… you will forget it.

scenes.img: A great royal tournament arena full of spectators: Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti strides in with his bow raised, every eye on him, banners flying.
scenes.text: Years later, at a great tournament, Karna walked into the arena… and matched every feat of the prince Arjuna.

scenes.img: In the arena, Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti lowers his bow and his head, as an elder in white points at him questioning, and the crowd laughs and jeers.
scenes.text: Then came the question. Who is your father? What is your family? And Karna lowered his bow… because the answer was a charioteer.

scenes.img: In the arena, Duryodhana: proud prince, thick black moustache, heavy gold crown, dark green and gold robes, gold mace places a gold crown on the head of Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti, crowning him king, the two clasping arms as friends.
scenes.text: Then prince Duryodhana stood up, and made Karna a king, of the land of Anga, right there and then. From that day, Karna was his friend for life.

scenes.img: At a riverbank at dawn, Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti holds out the gold armour plate he has just cut from his own chest, offering it to an old brahmin with a staff, who is the god Indra in disguise; a faint glow behind the brahmin.
scenes.text: Karna never refused anyone who asked. When the god Indra came disguised as a brahmin and asked for his golden armour and earrings… Karna cut them from his own body, and gave them.

scenes.img: By a chariot, Krishna: blue-skinned young man, clean-shaven, long black curly hair, tall gold crown with one peacock feather, yellow silk dhoti and a jewelled royal shawl, white-and-marigold flower garland, white U-shaped tilak rests a hand on the shoulder of Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti, speaking to him earnestly; Karna listens, stunned.
scenes.text: Before the war, Krishna told Karna the secret. You are Kunti’s eldest son. The Pandavas are your brothers. Come with them… and you will be king.

scenes.img: At a river at sunrise, Kunti: gentle royal woman, plain white sari, grey in her hair reaches out to Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti, who stands in the shallow water after his prayer to the Sun; both have tears in their eyes.
scenes.text: Then Kunti herself came to him at the river, where he prayed to the Sun. For the first time… his mother called him son.

scenes.img: Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti stands tall and firm at the river, one hand on his heart, gently refusing Kunti: gentle royal woman, plain white sari, grey in her hair, who bows her head.
scenes.text: Karna said no. Duryodhana stood by me when no one else did. I will not leave him now. But he made his mother a promise: of your sons… I will face only Arjuna.

scenes.img: Sunset on a battlefield: the wheel of a war chariot is sunk deep in the mud, and Karna: tall young warrior, dark-brown skin, clean-shaven, long black hair, a gold armour plate grown onto his chest and large gold sun-shaped earrings, red dhoti strains to lift it with both hands, alone, his bow on the ground.
scenes.text: In the war, his chariot wheel sank into the earth… and his learning left him, as the curse had said. And Karna fell.
The world kept asking Karna where he came from. Krishna only asked him… to see who he truly was.
Krishna says in the Gita… The wise see the same in a learned priest, a cow, an elephant, a dog… and the one the world calls an outcaste.
